correctness.rationale: Closed five-bit overlap paths are in bijection with indexed words tested in their two-sided periodic extensions, even when n<6. Although the frozen rule checks the first two length-four windows of each edge rather than all three, every position is tested along a closed path; it would be misleading to read the prose as a claim about checking the last length-four window of an isolated edge. Independently rebuilding with all three windows gave the same 16-state cyclic component and the same signed quotient determinants by integer Newton identities. The traces match all 18 stated counts and direct word enumeration agrees through n=14. Möbius inversion counts least-period indexed points, divided by n for primitive rotation orbits. Counts exclude 1,2,3,7; distinct least-period-4 and least-period-6 points account for all counted points at 8 (only period 4) and 12 (both). The three displayed 4-, 5- and 6-loops are simple returns to 10001. A smaller period of a concatenation would rotate its marker occurrences and periodically repeat the cyclic itinerary. A single length-5 loop for odd n≥9, a single length-6 loop for n≡2 mod 4 with n≥10, or a single block of two length-6 loops for n≡0 mod 4 with n≥16 gives an itinerary with no nontrivial rotation. These constructions cover the entire positive support. Strong connectivity and the coprime loops of lengths 4 and 5 give primitivity, the Parry measure is unique, and the Perron root lies in the unsigned factor by complement symmetry. Its reproduced decimal is 1.4012683679398549151…, and the trace asymptotic has leading coefficient one.
residual_risks: Finite counts establish the short exceptions, not the unbounded positive spectrum; the marker construction supplies that argument. Squares of half-length one are allowed; no quotient by complementation or reversal is taken.
